title: Phase159 hardening repairs (from the Phase158 revision-2 self-audit)

provenance_of_findings.audit: PHASE158_REV2_AUDIT_REPORT.md (16/16 PASS) executed 2026-10-17 against the sealed revision-2 archive sha256 b283332a8b8651e2d3e82acdf8b958bb1df43f5979dce905d9c0312778676beb
provenance_of_findings.machine_readable: PHASE158_REV2_AUDIT_FINDINGS.json (beside the delivery, outside the package)
provenance_of_findings.rule: repairs were forbidden on the sealed revision-2 tree; every finding recorded there was addressed by this new Phase159 tree instead, never by editing sealed bytes

repairs.finding: the secret scanner decoded files with encoding='utf-8', so a UTF-8 BOM on line 1 hid the first line's assignment from the ^-anchored credential rules (U+FEFF is not whitespace); the r2 audit demonstrated the blind spot with a BOM'd .env planted in a scratch tree
repairs.root_cause: Windows tools commonly write BOM-prefixed text; the scanner's line reader assumed BOM-less UTF-8
repairs.fix: scripts/security/scan_secrets.py decodes every scannable file with encoding='utf-8-sig' (strips a leading BOM; BOM-less files decode identically); a phase159 comment records why
repairs.test_strength: the fixture asserts the file bytes actually carry the BOM (efbbbf) before scanning, so the regression cannot silently pass against a BOM-less file

repairs.finding: a manifest-listed file absent from disk was reported with the inverted label 'manifest-extra:' (it reads as if the disk had an extra file); detection existed but the label misdescribed the failure to the operator
repairs.root_cause: the first diff loop appended the wrong label and the second loop's elif branch compensated by appending nothing for the same file; the pair produced exactly one inverted-label problem per missing file
repairs.fix: scripts/generate_manifest.py now reports the same condition as 'missing:'; the redundant elif branch was removed (dead after the rename); the docstring records the label vocabulary: 'missing:' = listed-but-absent, 'uncovered:' = on-disk-but-not-covered; detection is unchanged, wording only
tests_changed: tests/test_phase158_manifest_contract.py::TestVerifierProblems::test_missing_file_is_detected strengthened to assert the exact 'missing:b.txt' label and to forbid the inverted 'manifest-extra:' label

repairs.finding: tests/test_phase158_privacy_contract.py embedded a real historical venue order id as fixture data (the ten-digit value is recorded in the revision-2 audit materials beside the delivery, deliberately not reproduced in this package because an aggregate artifact carrying a harvested id is exactly what the privacy scanner flags); harmless to the scanner's operation but test fixtures should not carry real identifiers
repairs.root_cause: the fixture was copied from a genuine capture id during the Phase158 privacy-contract authoring
repairs.fix: all 10 fixture occurrences replaced with the synthetic id 9000001234, verified to collide with no harvested capture id; a comment in the test states the rule: fixture ids must be synthetic, never harvested
tests_changed: tests/test_phase158_privacy_contract.py (fixture ids only; scanner behavioral assertions untouched)
repairs.collisions_checked: 9000001234 does not appear anywhere under research/captures/ (checked by regex over the harvested order_id/client_order_id values)

hardening_alongside.what: scripts/security/scan_privacy.py reads every scanned line with encoding='utf-8-sig' — same BOM blind spot existed in the privacy scanner's line reader, closed alongside the secret-scanner fix

verification.focused: tests/test_phase158_privacy_contract.py + tests/test_secret_scan_phase0.py + tests/test_phase158_manifest_contract.py + tests/test_packaging_no_secrets_phase132.py: 34 passed (the 5 failures seen before the manifest regeneration were the stale-manifest class — the tree's BUILD_MANIFEST.sha256 still described the revision-2 bytes at that moment)
verification.full_suite: executed twice on the sealed candidate bytes (worktree and extraction runs), recorded in reports/PHASE159_FULL_SUITE_RUN.txt and the post-build bundle

next_time: any future revision starting from this tree must re-derive its own diff vs the Phase159 archive and re-run both scanners and the manifest contract from scratch
